en.title: Tantrums at Ages Two and Three: Understanding and Prevention
en.description: Nine daily lessons for the father and mother with a child aged two or three: understanding tantrums, noticing hunger, tiredness and transitions, safety with few words during a tantrum, closeness and naming feelings after the child calms down, understanding the repeated «no» with a few clear limits, offering two acceptable choices instead of one order, handling hitting and biting, preparing for a tantrum at the market or in front of guests, and calming your own anger and asking for help, with a calm response that keeps the child safe and meets the child's needs.

paths.band_notes: Ages 2-3: self-regulation and communication are developing. No deterministic diagnosis, guaranteed prevention, punishment, hitting or shaming. Safety, hunger, pain and distress must always be addressed. This recovery publishes only the first nine contiguous lessons; the remaining original drafts (s10) stay held in the preserved backup. The unit d7a09c7e-769c-48b5-aaf8-0511fedfc0db is not used (no source URL; invented quarter-hour and five-a-day thresholds). Units 179d90e1-a863-42e1-8fea-e8560b7401f7 (no source URL; 'suppression postpones the confrontation to adolescence' and a six-month threshold) and seed-defiance-23 (no exact source mapping; a non-verbatim prophetic saying) are not used by lessons 5 and 6. The unit d7a09c7e-769c-48b5-aaf8-0511fedfc0db, to which the backup draft of lesson 8 was pinned, is not used by lesson 8 either. Lesson 3 (during the tantrum) follows AAP HealthyChildren (do not ignore hitting, kicking, biting or throwing; stop it immediately; hold a child rushing into danger; no spanking, yelling or shaming; parent's own time-out with the child in a safe place), AACAP (tired, hungry, pain or mild illness; remain calm, you are modeling; state calmly which behavior must stop; never respond with physical aggression; seek help for danger, self-harm on purpose, not able to calm down, very frequent or longer than expected for age, getting in the way of life), CDC (ensure safety first; remain close, hands free, time and space to calm; ignoring only for minor, safe, attention-seeking behavior such as whining, never needs-based, distress or danger, child not left alone unless safe, attention returned when it stops; giving in rewards the tantrum; a pause or another trusted caregiver for the parent; lost skills -> talk with the doctor) and NHS (losing your temper or shouting back will not end it; do not change your mind or bribe with sweets; distraction; holding a child who is more upset than angry, when you are calm). No duration or count threshold is given. Lesson 4 (after the tantrum): CDC emotion coaching (wait until both are calm; pause and breathe; connect with eye contact, a smile or gentle touch; name the emotion in simple words, 'it seems like you are upset' when unsure, accept the child's correction and expand; validate feelings but limit behavior, then simple choices; rushing to solutions can dismiss feelings and escalate; teach acceptable ways to show upset; return to being positive and praise), NHS (do not hit back; make clear that hitting hurts and you will not allow it; 'I know you're feeling angry' helps a child name feelings; praise and cuddles), AAP (hug and start over; no shaming; consult the pediatrician if very withdrawn, persistently sad or highly demanding most of the time). No withdrawal of love, no grudges; referral and urgent-help sentence as in lesson 3. Lesson 5 (the repeated 'no'): CDC (the 'terrible twos' as toddlers begin to assert their independence; developing independence can look like pushing away, parents may feel frustrated or rejected, this is normal, pause; adjust expectations; routines and rules with consistency, predictability and follow-through; positive elements such as a bath toy or bubbles for a resisted routine; specific labeled praise), AAP HealthyChildren (two-year-olds test limits; consistently set reasonable limits that allow exploring, draw the line at dangerous or antisocial behavior; choose your battles and accommodate when you can, consistency is key; directed choices rather than yes/no questions; praise when they dress or feed themselves; no spanking, yelling or shaming; consult the pediatrician if very passive or withdrawn, persistently sad, or highly demanding and unsatisfied most of the time) and NHS (difficult behaviour often from tiredness, hunger, frustration or boredom; consistency, everyone close to the child responds the same way; explain why, e.g. holding hands to cross the road; specific praise; a reward before the behaviour is a bribe; smacking teaches hitting is OK) and AACAP (tired, hungry, pain or mild illness; remain calm; seek help for danger, self-harm, not calming, very frequent or longer than expected, getting in the way of life). Neither 'no' nor stubbornness is called a diagnosis; no breaking the will, no claim of later confrontation, no month or count threshold. Lesson 6 (two choices): AAP (give control over little things with small directed choices rather than yes/no questions; choices among acceptable alternatives with sensible limits; prepare children for upcoming activities), CDC (simple choices such as carrots or an apple; car seat buckled every ride, so safety is not offered as a choice; predictability and follow-through, do what you say; explain changes calmly; labeled praise) and NHS (consistency; no bribes). Choices are a help, not a guarantee; if they choose neither, check needs first, then the parent calmly decides and follows through without a long negotiation, shouting or threats. Lesson 7 (hitting and biting): AAP HealthyChildren (toddlers may lack self-control and lash out, hitting or biting in frustration; teach them to express feelings in words; avoid threats; praise gentle, kind behaviour; supervise and step in, pull the children apart and keep them separate until calm; teach saying 'no' firmly, turning away; control your own temper; consult the pediatrician for injury to self or others such as teeth marks or bruises, being barred from play, or fear for the safety of others; do not ignore hitting, kicking, biting or throwing, stop it immediately), AACAP Fighting and Biting (say no calmly but firmly; for two- to three-year-olds 'biting is not okay because it hurts people'; do not bite back; act early when the child is very frustrated; supervise; separate, comfort and attend to the other child first, then 'I know you are angry, but don't hit. Hitting hurts.'; do not hit a child who hits; a child who gets the toy by pushing is unintentionally rewarded; teething, unhappy, anxious; frequent or severe aggression or persistent biting -> professional evaluation), NHS (most young children occasionally bite, hit or push; this does not mean they will grow up aggressive; do not hit, bite or kick back; make clear it hurts and you will not allow it; praise and cuddles when they are not behaving badly) and CDC (hurting others is never ignored and is stopped immediately; yelling or embarrassing is unhealthy negative attention). The five-minute withdrawal of attention (AACAP), time-out, the 'few weeks' and 'month' figures (AAP) and the 'stay strong, do not apologize' advice are not used. Lesson 8 (a tantrum at the market or in front of guests): NHS (tantrums often happen in shops and embarrassment makes staying calm harder; keep trips short, involve the child by talking about what you need and letting them help; distraction; ignore the looks and concentrate on staying calm; losing your temper or shouting back will not end it; do not change your mind or bribe with sweets; tired or hungry first), AAP (a healthy snack when out; prioritize sleep even if you miss things; distraction, move to a new room; do not ignore hitting or biting; take turns with another adult when your frustration escalates), CDC (play eye-spy during errands, point to blue things; explain changes calmly; giving in at the grocery store; spanking, yelling at or embarrassing your child is unhealthy; praise 'thank you for being patient and staying by me'; help a three-year-old be ready for new places and meeting new people; the child is not left alone unless safe) and AACAP (tired, hungry, pain or mild illness; referral). No claim that other onlookers are parents, no promise that preparation prevents tantrums, no car as a place to leave the child. Lesson 9 (the parent's own anger): CDC (parenting is hard work, negative emotions are common; feeling frustrated or rejected is normal; notice and manage your own emotions and pause; a pause can be a few deep breaths; with no immediate safety concern it is fine to sit quietly together and return later; a longer pause such as a walk only with the child cared for by another trusted caregiver; children imitate, invite them to breathe with you; practice self-care), AAP HealthyChildren (control your own temper, expressed calmly your child will probably follow your example; give yourself a break and take turns with another parent or friend; if you made a real mistake in the heat of the moment, wait to cool down, apologize, explain how you will handle it next time and keep the promise; yelling, shaming and physical punishment are ineffective and harmful; calm your own stress first, be kind to yourself, both doing the best you can; if you are having a hard time reach out for more help), NHS (anger and frustration build up; get support from a partner, friend or another parent; children notice when you are upset and may behave badly when you are least able to cope, do not blame yourself or your child; do not feel you have to cope alone; contact your GP for yourself; talk to a health visitor if you are struggling with your mental health; support exists in a crisis or emergency). The backup draft's unit 6100b911-911d-4926-8f35-09b43a76303f (app-authored, no source; 'thirty seconds'; leaving the room) and placeholder h_004 are not used: no religious text, so the lesson carries no pending scholar review. No body-sign list, no time figure.

lessons.title: لماذا يغضب بهذه القوة؟
lessons.focus: Understand common toddler frustration while assessing needs and safety; calm support without labels or guarantees.

lessons.title: قبل النوبة: الجوع والنعاس والانتقال المفاجئ
lessons.focus: Notice hunger, tiredness and difficult transitions; predictable feeding/sleep routines and simple choices, without guaranteed prevention or fixed countdowns.

lessons.title: أثناء النوبة: أمانٌ وكلماتٌ قليلة
lessons.focus: During a tantrum: safety first (move harmful things away; stop hitting, biting, kicking, throwing or self-harm at once, calmly and without violence; hold a child rushing into danger); check tiredness, hunger, pain or illness and meet the need; stay close, give time to calm, few calm words; do not shout, hit, threaten or humiliate; a gentle hug if more sad than angry; do not give in or bribe after a reasoned no; turn attention away only from minor safe attention-seeking behaviour such as whining, while watching, never from need, pain, illness, fear or distress; parent's own pause with the child safe or with a trusted adult; referral and urgent help without numeric thresholds.

lessons.title: بعد أن يهدأ: الحضن أولًا ثم الكلمات
lessons.focus: After the tantrum: both calm first; closeness before words (hug if the child wants it, gentle touch, eye contact and a smile); name the feeling simply, accept correction; validate the feeling and limit the behaviour without a lecture, offer two simple choices; teach an acceptable way to say they are upset; do not rush to solutions; if they hit, say clearly that hitting hurts and is not allowed, never hit back; no shaming, return to the day warmly and praise words over screaming; referral (very frequent, longer than expected, cannot calm, harm, lost skills, persistently sad or withdrawn) and urgent help.

lessons.title: «لا» الصغيرة: العناد علامة نموّ
lessons.focus: The repeated 'no' at two and three: part of growing independence and testing limits, not a verdict on child or parent; check tiredness, hunger, frustration or boredom first; a few clear, consistent limits for safety and harm, explained simply, flexible on small matters; say what will happen as a calm statement instead of a yes/no question when 'no' is not an option; make a resisted routine more fun; everyone responds the same way and follows through; specific praise for cooperation; never hit, shout, threaten or shame; the parent's own pause; referral and urgent help without numeric thresholds.

lessons.title: خياران بدل أمرٍ واحد
lessons.focus: Offering two choices that are both acceptable to the parent instead of a yes/no question or a bare order (control over little things); no choice where safety is concerned, such as the car seat: state it calmly and do it; tell them beforehand what will happen next; if they choose neither, check needs, then the parent decides calmly and follows through without long negotiation; specific praise; choices help but do not guarantee cooperation; no bribes, shouting or threats.

lessons.title: حين يضرب أو يعضّ
lessons.focus: Hitting and biting at two and three: common because self-control and words are still developing, occasional hitting is not a verdict; never ignored: stop it at once, calmly and firmly, separate the children and stay close; comfort the hurt child first, then 'I know you are angry, but no hitting. Hitting hurts.'; the toy is not won by hitting; never hit or bite back, no shouting, threats or humiliation; parent's pause close by or with a trusted adult; teach words and walking away, step in early, check hunger, tiredness, teething pain, worry or sadness; specific praise and affection; referral (frequent or severe, injuries, fear for others' safety, kept from play, self-harm, persistent sadness) and urgent help without numeric thresholds.

lessons.title: نوبةٌ في السوق أو أمام الضيوف
lessons.focus: Tantrums in public: embarrassment is understandable and makes calm harder; prepare (not hungry or tired, sleep first, a healthy snack, short trips, say beforehand what will and will not be bought, involve the child, a small game, prepare for guests or new places); during: needs first, distraction, hold a reasoned no without buying or promising sweets, move calmly to a quieter place and stay with the child, ignore the looks, no hitting, shouting, threats or embarrassing; stop hitting, biting or danger at once; a trusted adult can take over; afterwards no long reckoning, specific praise for calm outings; referral and urgent help without numeric thresholds. Preparation helps but is not a guarantee.

lessons.title: حين تنفد طاقتك أنت
lessons.focus: The parent's own anger with a toddler: negative feelings are common and do not make a bad parent; the child learns from how the parent handles anger; notice upset early and pause with a few deep breaths; sit quietly together when there is no danger; a longer pause only with a trusted adult caring for the child, never leaving the child alone; breathe together; look at what weighs on the day, do not blame yourself or the child, ask partner, friend or another parent for help and take turns; be gentle with yourself; after a real mistake, calm down, apologize, say what you will do next time and keep it; no hitting, shouting or humiliation; talk with a doctor or specialist if anger often escapes control or the parent is sad, worn out or anxious most of the time; urgent help with a trusted adult staying with the child if the parent fears hurting the child or themselves. No religious text; no time figures.
